ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $AC=6$, $BC=8$. Point $D$ is on side $AB$, $DE \perp AC$, and $DF \perp BC$ with the feet of the perpendiculars being points $E$ and $F$, respectively. Join $EF$. What is the minimal value of segment $EF$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a right triangle ABC, C is at the lower left, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower right, AC is vertical, BC is horizontal, and ∠C=90°. Point D is on the hypotenuse AB; from D, perpendiculars are drawn respectively to AC and BC, with feet E and F, so quadrilateral CEDF is a rectangle. Thus EF is one diagonal of this rectangle, and CD is the other diagonal, so EF=CD. Now when D moves on AB, requiring EF to be minimal is just requiring CD to be minimal; this is equivalent to finding the shortest distance from point C to line AB, namely the altitude from C to AB. From AC=6 and BC=8, get AB=10. The area of the triangle is (1/2)·6·8=24, and it is also equal to (1/2)·10·h, so h=24·2/10=4.8. Therefore the minimum value of EF is 4.8.
